4c8f08746603574b: SINGAPORE: The global economy is under threat from persistently high energy prices, record public debt and risks from the AI investment boom, International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Wednesday, urging governments to take protective fiscal and monetary policy measures.

In a speech previewing IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings next week in Bangkok, Georgieva said the world was being pulled in two directions -- a negative energy supply shock from the Middle East conflicts and a positive demand shock from artificial intelligence that is also fuelling inflation.
"The combined impact of these two forces is highly uneven across the world," Georgieva said, adding that the AI boom was bypassing many countries.

New IMF growth forecasts to be released during the Bangkok meetings will show the biggest growth downgrades will come in economies ravaged by war, Georgieva said. These include Ukraine, suffering significant damage to civilian and economic infrastructure, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.
Georgieva did not indicate in her prepared remarks whether the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook would change the overall 2026 global growth forecast from the sluggish 3.0% rate forecast in July.

That forecast, which predicted a rebound to 3.4% growth in 2027, assumed the Strait of Hormuz would start to reopen in mid-July and return to pre-war conditions by March 2027. It assumed oil prices would average US$89 a barrel in 2026 and US$78 a barrel in 2027.

Georgieva said oil prices remain at US$100 a barrel, with impaired refining capacity adding another US$100 in "crack-spread" margins per barrel for key products including diesel. The winter heating season will boost demand as natural gas supplies remain restricted by threats to LNG shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, she added.

"Even if the war in the Gulf were to end soon, the problem of high energy prices will likely persist for some time," Georgieva said, adding that Brent crude oil futures LCOc1 predict high oil prices through 2027.

Higher energy prices are pushing up inflation, policy rates and benchmark bond yields, she said, noting that US, German and Japanese 10-year sovereign yields are now at their highest levels since 2007, 2009 and 1996, respectively, and still climbing.
Growing debt load

Adding to the worries to be discussed by the IMF's 191 member countries next week is a growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures, Georgieva said. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and is projected to exceed 100% of GDP before 2030.
Georgieva singled out advanced economies, led by the US, as the "worst offenders" on debt loads, with debt-to-GDP ratios higher than emerging markets and low income countries.
Policymakers can no longer rely on higher growth rates alone to solve fiscal problems, she said.

"And yet we don't see decisive action in the high-debt advanced economies where the need of the hour is for credible medium-term fiscal consolidation plans, supported in some cases by upfront fiscal measures, including to take some pressure off monetary policy," she said.

After five-and-a-half years of above-target inflation, Georgieva said inflationary pressures were persisting, from the AI build-out, energy and food price shocks, tariffs, higher defense spending and higher debt service costs.

"Now may be a good time for a prudently hawkish bias in many countries' monetary policy," Georgieva said, adding that rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve, the ECB and the Bank of Japan were "highly appropriate."
AI risks abound
Georgieva highlighted other risks from AI, where investment as a share of GDP is likely to exceed that of railroads, the electricity grids or telecommunications infrastructure.

The rising economic and financial concentration puts pressure on AI companies to deliver productivity and earnings gains to justify lofty valuations, she said, warning that market disappointment could turn into "a far-reaching shock."
But she said IMF research suggests that AI, done right, could add a half percentage point of extra world growth annually.

AI preparedness is key, she said, including regulatory guardrails that "help manage AI's substantial perils, which include large-scale labour market fallout, serious cyber and stability risks and frontier models threatening to escape human control and run amok."

In addition to building fiscal strength, even at difficult political costs, Georgieva said governments should take other steps to boost growth, including reforms that would develop improved workforce skills, make corporate start-ups and wind-downs easier, boost energy security and streamline regulations.
7bb2b7e4930188cb: MELAKA, Oct 7 — The Election Commission (EC) today announced November 14 for polling in the 16th Melaka state election, and set the nomination for Oct 31.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said early voting had been set for November 10 and the campaign period would run for 14 days.
He said this at a press conference after chairing a special meeting to determine the date for the state election here.

Regarding the Electoral Roll (DPPR) that will be used in the 16th Melaka state election (PRN), Ramlan said that a total of 687,697 voters, consisting of 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel, are eligible to vote in the state election.

For postal voting matters, applications for both domestic and international categories have been open since Sept 23, and the deadline for postal voting applications for Category 1A, which includes election staff, EC officers, military personnel, and media, is set for Oct 28.
“For Category 1B, which is Malaysian citizens abroad, and 1C, which is for agencies or organisations, the deadline is on Oct 23,” he said.
Commenting further, Ramlan said the EC appointed 28 returning officers and 80 assistant returning officers.

He said that to monitor election campaign activities throughout the official campaigning period, the EC will establish 28 Election Campaign Enforcement Teams (PP-KPR), including representatives from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities (PBT), and representatives of contesting candidates.
“A total of 28 candidate nomination centres (PPC) and official vote counting centres (PPRU) will be used in this election, while 11,175 personnel will be appointed to manage the process.

“A total of 271 polling centres with 1,263 channels will be opened, involving 31 early voting centres with 50 early voting channels and 240 regular polling centres with 1,213 channels,” he said, adding that the allocation for conducting the Melaka state election is estimated at RM28.45 million.

He said the EC is also offering government agencies and non-governmental organisations (NGO) to be election observers to monitor the Melaka state election process from nomination day until the election results are announced.
“They are allowed to make observations at the PPC, polling centres, counting centres and PPRU, and must comply with all the appointment conditions set by the EC.”
Further information and application forms related to election observers can be obtained from the SPR Portal www.spr.gov.my starting from Oct 7, 2026 (today) and until Oct 21, 2026. — Bernama
d687aafd7b7fe42d: PETALING JAYA: Follow-up action on audits by the national audit department resulted in revenue collection and repayments totalling RM920.91 million as of Sept 28, says law and institutional reform minister Azalina Othman Said.
She said the figure demonstrated that audits are effective when findings are followed by appropriate action.

"It proves that audits followed by action can result in the tangible recovery of public funds," she was quoted as saying by Bernama during the tabling of the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Azalina said ministries, departments and agencies should not view audit findings as "attacks", but as an opportunity to rectify weaknesses, improve systems and safeguard public funds.

She said the report tabled on Oct 5 contained 38 recommendations and required follow-up action to identify those responsible for weaknesses, corrective measures, completion timelines and methods for monitoring progress.
"Audits must lead to action. Findings must lead to corrective measures. Weaknesses must lead to improvements," she said.
Azalina also urged state assemblies to allow the report to be examined and debated openly, not just tabled.
6a04799ecfa55a36: KUALA LUMPUR: The Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court (PKPMP) will be required to meet the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) within two months to respond to its recommendations on the e-Jamin bail system.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin told the New Straits Times that the Chief Registrar would have two months to respond to all the recommendations outlined by the committee.
"Within two months, they need to come to the PAC to provide feedback on all the recommendations that have been given," she said.

In Parliament today, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said also said the Chief Registrar should respond to the committee's concerns over the e-Jamin bail system.
Azalina said e-Jamin falls under the courts' purview and questions about its current status should be directed to the Chief Registrar.
She said the Chief Registrar had been informed and may issue a statement.
The PAC had earlier recommended eight measures to safeguard bail funds, including for PKPMP and the Finance Ministry to expedite negotiations with Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd to finalise a formal agreement.
It also said the government must finalise the definition of "public money" to avoid confusion among government agencies.
The committee recommended that PKPMP develop its own internal bail module through eCF (eCourt Finance) or e-Kehakiman to reduce dependence on vendors and ensure full government ownership of the data.
It also said the Finance Ministry, Attorney-General's Chambers and Digital Department must strengthen ICT procurement controls to prevent vendors from operating without valid contracts.
The PAC further recommended that the Finance Ministry tighten the granting of special financial exemptions to uphold good governance.

PAC's report, tabled on Oct 5, revealed that the e-Jamin system had operated for five years without a formal government contract, raising concerns over the handling of bail deposits, including funds held in the operator's commercial accounts.
The e-Jamin court bill payment system was designed to allow a bailor or surety to complete court bail payments on behalf of an accused person.
Mas Ermieyati said the system had operated across 192 courts nationwide since Jan 10, 2020 without a formal contractual agreement with the Federal government.
Of the RM193.71 million in bail deposits held in the account as at Dec 31, 2024, Dapat Vista was found to have invested RM130.8 million under the company's name.
The system also had no Letter of Appointment, Letter of Acceptance, Letter of Intent or formal contract with the Government throughout that period.

The committee found that bail payments were held in the operator's commercial accounts instead of the Government's Consolidated Trust Account, breaching Article 97(1) of the Federal Constitution and Section 7 of the Financial Procedure Act 1957.

It also raised concerns over the absence of a trustee arrangement, performance bond and insurance, as well as an unreconciled RM557,258 difference between system records and the operator's bank statements.
Mas Ermieyati also noted the government already had alternative channels for managing bail, including the eCourt Finance system, electronic fund transfers and the iPayment system.

6c528586f432dcf0: SEOUL: South Korea's president said Wednesday the country is taking steps to protect the country's booming cultural cache, launching a new "K-brand" authentication system that will let consumers know if goods they are purchasing are the real deal.

Led by K-pop acts such as BTS, hit Netflix series "Squid Game" and "KPop Demon Hunters", the so-called "Hallyu", or Korean cultural wave, saw content exports hit a record US$14.9 billion last year, surpassing overseas sales of computers and home appliances.

The popularity of so-called K-food and K-beauty products, meanwhile, saw exports of agricultural and fisheries products and cosmetics hit record highs of US$12.4 billion and US$11.4 billion, respectively.

Under Seoul's new "K-Brand Government Certification System", consumers will now be able to check whether a product is authentic by scanning a QR code attached to it with their mobile phone, president Lee Jae Myung said Wednesday.
"From K-beauty and K-food to K-fashion, Korean brands are rapidly becoming part of the everyday lives of people around the world," Lee said on X.
"But as K-brands grow in popularity, Korean companies are also suffering increasing damage from counterfeit products overseas," he said.
"The government will respond swiftly to counterfeit products overseas," Lee said, adding that it would "no longer leave our companies to fight alone".
Thirty-one companies have already signed up for the scheme, including Samyang Foods, the maker of Buldak spicy chicken ramen, and Amorepacific, South Korea's largest cosmetics company.
According to data released by the OECD in 2024, the global market for counterfeit "K-brand" products was approximately ₩11 trillion (US$8.2 billion).
The love of all things Korean has also impacted arrivals to the country, with the number of foreign tourists hitting an all-time high of 18.94 million last year.
9e91b6f6798c78af: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Four Undangs or traditional ruling chiefs of Negeri Sembilan — including three disputed ones — today dropped their court attempt in Kuala Lumpur to ultimately remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Negeri Sembilan ruler.

Today, the four men — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin — applied to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur to withdraw their court case against the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar and the Negeri Sembilan state government.

In their court case filed in July via judicial review, the four men had wanted the court to order the Menteri Besar to sign — within seven days of the court order — their April 19 declaration to “sack” Tuanku Muhriz as Negeri Sembilan ruler.
The April 19 declaration document also contains the four men's declaration that they had selected and appointed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the new Negeri Sembilan ruler.
They had also wanted the court to declare that the April 19 declaration is a valid document according to the Negeri Sembilan state constitution.
But after the four men applied to drop the case, the High Court in Kuala Lumpur today also decided that the dropped case cannot be filed again.

When contacted, lawyer Steven Thiru confirmed to Malay Mail that the four men had dropped the case in the Kuala Lumpur courts, but said they did not give any reason to the court for the case withdrawal.
Steven was representing the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and the DKU secretary, two of the proposed interveners to the case.

There were four proposed interveners or four parties who were applying to join the court case, namely the DKU, DKU secretary, the current Sungei Ujong Undang Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and current Rembau Undang Datuk Hassan Ab. Hamid.

In explaining what happened in open court today before High Court judge Norliza Othman, Steven said the four men had asked to withdraw the court case with no order on legal costs, while the Attorney-General’s Chambers had agreed to the withdrawal with no order as to costs.

Steven said that the four proposed interveners did not object to the withdrawal, but had asked the court to give order on costs, as the withdrawal of the judicial review would mean that the case had no merits.
“Importantly, the judicial review in the Kuala Lumpur High Court was an abuse of process,” he told Malay Mail.

Steven said the four men’s court case was an abuse of court process, as they did not disclose these key facts to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur: that there was a pending court proceeding in the High Court in Seremban that they had already started with two other individuals, as well as the High Court in Seremban’s June 5 injunction order and July 8 order for leave for contempt of court which the DKU and DKU secretary had obtained.
Steven said the four men’s act of filing a court case in Kuala Lumpur on July 17 when they already had an ongoing case in Seremban amounted to “forum shopping”.
“Forum shopping” is known as the act of shopping around or looking for a court which would most likely decide in their favour.
“This was a clear case of forum shopping, as well as suppression of material facts from the Kuala Lumpur High Court in the judicial review which was filed on July 17, 2026,” he said.
Steven said the High Court today ultimately ordered the four men to pay RM40,000 in costs, namely RM10,000 to each of the four proposed interveners.
He also confirmed that the High Court decided that the four have no liberty to file afresh or cannot file the same court case again.

On August 1, the DKU announced that these three individuals — Mubarak, Abdul Rahim, and Maarof — had either ceased to hold or never lawfully held the positions of Undang for Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu.
The four men in today’s court are those three individuals, as well as Muhammed who is currently listed as the Johol Undang on the Negeri Sembilan state government’s website.
On August 1, the DKU formally recognised Muhammad Faris and Raja Hassan as the Undang for Sungei Ujong and Rembau, and said Maarof had been dismissed as Jelebu Undang.
The Negeri Sembilan state government’s website currently lists the Jelebu Undang position as vacant.
9619b4090984a4a0: PETALING JAYA: The federal government is failing to collect billions of ringgit owed to it, with only 5% of RM9.273 billion in outstanding debts recovered last year, says Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Karim.

Debating the 2026 Auditor-General's Report in the Dewan Rakyat, Hassan said the government’s weak debt collection was particularly concerning given that federal debt rose by 5.9% last year to RM1.321 trillion.
"The government is quite good at borrowing but not good at recovering debts," he said.
"What is the evidence? The auditor-general’s report shows that billions of ringgit in debts owed to the federal government by various parties have not been paid.
"Some debts have gone on for as long as 40 years without being settled... The report reveals that the federal government’s debt collection system has failed."
Hassan’s remarks come amid scrutiny over outstanding payments owed to government agencies.
On Monday, Zetrix AI Bhd, a subsidiary of MyEG Group, said it had submitted a proposed solution to the government to address RM314 million in arrears owed to the road transport department.

Transport minister Loke Siew Fook said the arrears involved fees and summonses collected by the company since May, adding that the ministry and JPJ would set a deadline for the amount to be settled and take appropriate steps to recover the funds.
Hassan also urged the government not to use taxpayers’ money to bailout loss-making government-linked companies or private firms, given the country’s high level of debt.
He alluded to a major national airline, saying he was informed that the company had RM18.4 billion in short-term debt and quarterly losses of RM830 million.
Hassan said the government should reject any request for financial assistance from the company.
"If this company knocks on the finance ministry’s door and asks for help, I hope the government rejects it because the government itself is in debt," he said.
"The government has other matters to deal with."
Hassan’s remarks appeared to refer to AirAsia, which last month denied that it was seeking a government bailout.
AirAsia Group co-founder and adviser Tony Fernandes said the airline’s operations remained sustainable and that it had never sought government assistance throughout its 25 years of operations.

He also dismissed reports that the government had approached rival carriers about absorbing some of AirAsia’s domestic routes, saying Putrajaya had confirmed to him that no such discussions took place.
84fbeaead4bf785c: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Ahli Parlimen mempersoalkan sama ada kapal tempur pesisir (LCS) Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia (TLDM) masih mampu memenuhi keperluan pertahanan apabila mencapai keupayaan operasi penuh, kira-kira 24 tahun selepas projek itu diluluskan pada 2011.
Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (LKAN) 2/2026 yang dikeluarkan Isnin lalu mendapati kapal pertama, LCS 1, mungkin hanya dapat beroperasi sepenuhnya pada Disember 2035.

Ketika membahaskan laporan itu di Dewan Rakyat hari ini, Chong Zhemin (PH-Kampar) mempersoalkan sama ada keupayaan LCS 1 masih dapat memenuhi keperluan operasi ketika itu susulan perubahan teknologi dan ancaman keselamatan.
“Dalam tempoh 24 tahun ini, berapa banyak teknologi dan ancaman keselamatan sudah berubah? Kita membeli kapal ini untuk menghadapi ancaman semasa.
“Adakah akhirnya kita akan menerima keupayaan yang direka untuk menghadapi ancaman masa lalu sedangkan ancaman sudah berubah?

“Lebih membimbangkan, penyerahan fizikal kapal tidak semestinya bermakna ia sudah mempunyai keupayaan tempur sepenuhnya. Kita mahukan kapal yang boleh digunakan dalam peperangan, bukan sekadar kapal yang boleh membawa penumpang.”
Beliau menggesa kerajaan membentangkan pelan pemulihan yang jelas, termasuk perincian mengenai pembekal, jadual pelaksanaan dan kos.

Chong turut menggesa Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi, yang menjadi menteri pertahanan ketika keputusan awal perolehan dibuat pada 2010 dan 2011, menjelaskan tanggungjawabnya terhadap keputusan berkenaan.
Katanya, tindakan perlu diambil terhadap sesiapa yang didapati melakukan salah laku tanpa mengira kedudukan atau fahaman politik.
“Pada 2010, arahan (Zahid) ialah ‘sila laksanakan’ projek ini. Pada 2026, rakyat masih bertanya: bila kita akan mendapat LCS yang mempunyai keupayaan tempur sepenuhnya?”
Chong turut menyokong gesaan supaya Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) ditubuhkan bagi menyiasat projek LCS.
Isnin lalu, LKAN 2/2026 mendapati projek LCS lewat 7.55% daripada jadual setakat 25 Jun, sekali gus menimbulkan risiko terhadap penyerahan fizikal LCS 1.
Kelewatan itu antaranya berpunca daripada sistem pelancar Naval Strike Missile (NSM) yang masih belum tersedia selepas permit eksportnya dibatalkan secara kekal oleh kerajaan Norway.

Ketua Audit Negara Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi dilaporkan berkata kelewatan antara 30 hingga 108 hari itu boleh menjejaskan tarikh penyerahan yang dijadualkan pada 26 Ogos atau sasaran disemak pada 26 Disember.

05983e96c269ffb7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Federal lawmaker Lim Guan Eng (Bagan - DAP) today again called on the government to consider the financial impact on small and medium businesses amid rumours it could raise the minimum wage when tabling Budget 2027, warning that abrupt hikes could disrupt long-term commercial agreements.
Lim, a former finance minister, argued that many enterprises operate under binding multi-year contracts where labor costs are fixed at agreed-upon rates.
“Many businesses have long-term contracts with foreign workers at agreed rates,” the DAP leader said at a press conference in Parliament this afternoon.
“A sudden wage increase would place an unexpected financial burden on employers.”

Lim, a former finance minister, noted that unexpected cost surges could strain operating margins and create operational friction for businesses unable to renegotiate existing contractual terms on short notice.
The former minister has been vocal in opposing the minimum wage hike and mandatory EPF contribution for foreign workers.

Lim claimed employers are often forced to hire foreign workers because it’s difficult to hire locals, particularly for SMEs, although his critics reject the argument as a “script” companies typically deploy to continue suppressing wages.

The former minister’s view closely aligns with the core arguments consistently raised by the Malaysian Employers Federation. The MEF generally opposes frequent or steep statutory minimum wage hikes across the board, favoring wage growth tied strictly “to productivity and market forces”.

Malaysian workers productivity have grown in the last 10 years, yet real wages grew at a fraction of that rate — averaging around 1 per cent annually, with periods of stagnant or declining purchasing power for private-sector employees, data from Bank Negara Malaysia and the Department of Statistics Malaysia showed.

Malaysia’s compensation of employees (CE) share of GDP, that is the portion of economic output paid out as wages, has historically lingered around 32 to 35 per cent, significantly below developed economies, data from the two bodies show.
This means greater share of value creation by Malaysian workers flows to capital returns, corporate profits, and reinvestment rather than payroll.
CE typically sits between 45 to 50 per cent in richer economies.

eaea5ca33aed02cb: KUALA LUMPUR: Local creative industry heavyweights are calling for continuous government funding and better payment rates for TV productions ahead of the upcoming national budget.
Datuk Yusof Haslam, vice-president of the Malaysian Film Producers Association (PFM), stressed that existing support must stay in place.
He warned that without it rising inflation and operating costs will hit the local entertainment scene hard.
"I hope the government views this positively and keeps all previous support for the industry. Any cuts should be avoided if possible," Yusof said in a recent Bernama report.
The veteran filmmaker also reminded grant recipients to manage their money properly and be honest.
"Filmmakers must be responsible, finish their films within the set budget, and take the job seriously. Do not use these funds for personal gain," he warned.

Yusof highlighted the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI), noting how essential it has been. Besides attracting big international film crews to the country, it has also helped fund ambitious local projects like 'MALBATT: Misi Bakara'.
However, he pointed out a major issue: TV payment rates have barely moved in decades, especially at state broadcaster Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM).

"I have been making TV dramas since 1985. Back then, a drama budget was around RM40,000. Nearly 40 years later, that rate has only gone up by about RM10,000. These figures should be reviewed every 10 years. If RTM raises its rates, private channels will naturally follow," he says.
Film producer Nazira Ibrahim shared similar concerns, adding that smaller local filmmakers urgently need help with marketing and distribution to reach wider audiences.

"We often have great stories, but we lack the right platforms to market and distribute them. Government help in building these channels would really boost Malaysian cinema both at home and abroad," Nazira said.
She also spoke about the RM10 million set aside for Creative Multimedia TVET MADANI.
Instead of keeping students in classrooms, Nazira believes hands-on experience on actual film sets is key to building real skills.

"Skills are not just for people in front of the camera, like actors, writers, and directors. The crew behind the scenes — camera operators, lighting teams, visual effects specialists, editor teams, and sound engineers — are just as important," she noted.
"Book learning is not enough. Trainees need real on-the-job training with working crews so they can see how a live set operates," Nazira added.

In the previous budget, the government allocated RM110 million in incentives for local and international filmmakers, including RM10 million specially reserved for national-themed projects to boost the creative economy.
The 2027 Budget will be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9.
339efad78a2297df: SINGAPORE, Oct 7 — Max Verstappen’s resurgence in Malaysia will be put to the test just 300 kilometres south at the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend, where the Red Bull driver may need to overcome the elements and his own poor record at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
An imperious Verstappen took his first chequered flag of the year at the wide open and fast Sepang Circuit at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.

But it was in a race delayed for an hour and a half after a chaotic formation lap saw cars, including Verstappen’s, grind to halt because of a software glitch in the settings for running in wet conditions.

“It was insane,” said Verstappen. “At some points, we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand it... I saw eight cars crawling and Lewis (Hamilton) stopped... It’s not what you want for the sport.”
Rain could again play a part in the tropical city state, with thunderstorms forecast to affect both Saturday’s sprint race and qualifying, and Sunday’s night grand prix.

Verstappen has never won at the twisty Marina Bay Street Circuit, where extremes of heat and humidity play a part in the most physically attritional race of the season on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.
Drivers can shed up to three kilogrammes (more than six pounds) during the longest outing on the calendar, where completing the 62 steamy laps often lasts the maximum two hours race time allowed.
A floor upgrade coupled with Verstappen finally working out how to get the best from the new generation car led him to call the result at Sepang four days ago “amazing”.
Runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second in the Mercedes and is likely to be challenging for the chequered flag again.

He was the beneficiary of yet more bad luck for his teammate and main title rival George Russell, who was “beyond disappointment” after an agonising power unit failure when running third with five laps to go in Malaysia.
“You’ve almost got to laugh... it’s just so many times this season it’s happened,” said Russell, who has failed to finish three times in 16 grands prix so far in 2026.

Lewis Hamilton has won four times in Singapore in the past and was buoyed by a drive at Sepang where he cut through the field to recover to third after starting on unsuitable dry tyres and dropping to the back.
“To finish on the podium after the way the race began feels really satisfying,” said Hamilton.
“It is a great reward for the hard work, determination and resilience everyone showed today.”
Russell won the Singapore Grand Prix a year ago, edging Verstappen and the current world champion Lando Norris of McLaren. — AFP
6f4b578a15e85e61: BRUSSELS: Brussels is considering taxing big US tech companies through a broad levy on large corporations in an effort to raise revenues for the EU while avoiding a backlash from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

The European Commission was working on new ways to capture more income from tech groups such as Apple, Meta and Google without singling them out, the newspaper reported, citing six officials with knowledge of the discussions.

Brussels was considering changes to its "Corporate Resource for Europe" (CORE) proposal that would require all companies operating in the EU with revenue of more than €100 million (US$112.32 million) a year to pay an annual lump-sum tax contribution, the report said.
In its current form, CORE requires these companies to pay a fixed annual levy of between €100,000 and €750,000, capturing only a small portion of a multinational company’s earnings.
"Some EU capitals are opposed to a pure digital tax because they don’t want to upset the Americans, and many more are opposed to CORE," an EU official told the FT.
"The solution is to expand (the tax) to cover pretty much all the big companies," the official said.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The European Commission, the Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA), which represents several US tech companies, Apple, Google and Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours.
US president Donald Trump in June threatened a 100% tariff on all goods from any country that imposes a digital services tax on American companies.

The US Trade Representative's office, which has long threatened European countries with retaliatory tariffs if they impose such taxes, has argued that these levies discriminate against US companies, which dominate the sector globally.
0d3952867d8c666b: PETALING JAYA: Polis menahan seorang lagi suspek dipercayai terbabit kes samun kedai emas di SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, membabitkan kerugian kira-kira RM1.75 juta.
Warga China berusia awal 40-an itu ditahan sejurus tiba di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur, semalam. Ini menjadikan tujuh individu diberkas setakat ini, termasuk lima warga asing.

Pemangku Ketua Polis Pahang, Azry Akmar Ayob, berkata suspek ditahan setibanya di Malaysia bagi membantu siasatan dan direman sehingga Sabtu ini, tetapi tiada barangan berkaitan kes itu dirampas daripadanya.

"Siasatan masih diteruskan dan baki suspek akan kita kesan serta tangkap," katanya menurut Berita Harian selepas Majlis Serah Terima Tugas Ketua Polis Bentong dan Pengerusi Perkep Bentong di IPD Bentong.

Ogos lalu, tiga lelaki bersenjatakan kapak dan kuku kambing dipercayai mengambil masa sekitar dua minit untuk melarikan 81 barang kemas kira-kira 2.5kg yang bernilai RM1.747 juta dari sebuah kedai emas di SkyAvenue.
Polis dilaporkan berkata, suspek memakai penutup muka, topi dan jaket sebelum mengumpil serta memecahkan cermin pameran barang kemas.
b1141d30a913294c: PUTRAJAYA: Kerajaan tidak boleh merampas keseluruhan wang dalam akaun bank hanya kerana sebahagian daripada wang itu dikaitkan dengan kegiatan jenayah, kata Mahkamah Rayuan.

Panel tiga hakim membenarkan sebahagian rayuan LWC Good Service Sdn Bhd terhadap perintah Mahkamah Tinggi yang merampas RM1.36 juta daripada dua akaun bank miliknya di bawah Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan dan Hasil Daripada Aktiviti Haram 2001 (Amla).
Rayuan itu didengar Hakim K Muniandy, Azman Abdullah dan Dean Wayne Daly.

Muniandy yang menyampaikan penghakiman sebulat suara, berkata pihak pendakwaan berjaya membuktikan jejak wang secara langsung yang menunjukkan pemindahan RM360,000 daripada sebuah 'akaun keldai' yang dikaitkan dengan penipuan pelaburan Comoncaps ke akaun Hong Leong Bank milik LWC Good Service.
Bagaimanapun katanya, tiada bukti yang mengaitkan baki wang berkenaan dengan penipuan itu.
Mahkamah memerintahkan RM360,000 dalam akaun Hong Leong Bank itu dirampas, tetapi mengarahkan RM863,179.84 dalam akaun sama dan RM139,329.24 dalam akaun CIMB milik LWC dipulangkan.
“Syak wasangka, walau sekuat atau seberat mana sekalipun, tidak boleh menggantikan bukti di sisi undang-undang,” kata Muniandy dalam alasan penghakiman bertulis.

Beliau berkata Amla tidak boleh dijadikan 'alat perampasan serba guna' yang membolehkan wang dirampas hanya kerana profil korporat sesebuah syarikat tidak teratur atau rakan niaganya tidak mematuhi keperluan kewangan.

Muniandy berkata perampasan wang yang tidak terbukti mempunyai kaitan dengan aktiviti haram akan menjadi 'pelucutan harta secara tidak berperlembagaan tanpa kuasa undang-undang' di bawah Perkara 13 Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
“Negara tidak boleh merampas baki akaun yang tidak berkaitan hanya berdasarkan syak wasangka, ketidakpatuhan atau percampuran wang tanpa kaitan pembuktian yang menjadi asas,” katanya.
Mahkamah berkata doktrin kebolehpisahan menghendaki wang yang terbukti tercemar dipisahkan daripada baki wang dalam akaun berkenaan.
LWC merupakan antara 28 responden dalam prosiding pelucuthakan sivil yang timbul daripada penipuan pelaburan Comoncaps, yang menyaksikan 22 mangsa didakwa kerugian kira-kira RM3.49 juta.
Mahkamah Tinggi sebelum ini memerintahkan keseluruhan baki RM1.223 juta dalam akaun Hong Leong Bank LWC dan RM139,329.24 dalam akaun CIMB dirampas.
Mahkamah Rayuan berkata Mahkamah Tinggi terkhilaf apabila gagal membezakan RM360,000 yang terbukti tercemar daripada baki wang dalam akaun berkenaan.
b4cb02cc89170d4d: PETALING JAYA: Kampar MP Chong Zhemin today asked whether the littoral combat ships (LCS) the navy ordered will still be useful by the time they achieve full operational capability, some 24 years after the project was approved in 2011.
The Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 released on Monday found that the navy’s first littoral combat ship (LCS 1) might not be fully operational until December 2035.
Debating the report in the Dewan Rakyat today, Chong asked whether LCS 1’s capabilities would meet operational needs, given changes in technology and security threats.
"How many technological changes and how many changes in security threats would have occured over these 24 years? We bought the ship to deal with current threats," he said.
"Will we end up with a capability designed for yesterday’s threats when the threats have already changed?
"More worrying, physical delivery does not necessarily mean that the ship has achieved full combat capability. We want a ship that can fight a war, not a ship that can merely carry passengers."
He urged the government to present a clear recovery plan, including details of the suppliers, schedule and costs.

Chong also called on deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who was defence minister when the initial procurement decisions were made in 2010 and 2011, to explain what responsibility he took for these decisions.
He said action should be taken against anyone found to have committed misconduct, regardless of position or political affiliation.
"In 2010, (Zahid's) instruction was ‘please implement’ (the project). In 2026, the people are still asking: when will we get an LCS with full combat capability?" he said.
Chong also backed calls for a royal commission of inquiry into the LCS project.
The auditor-general's report said LCS 1 could be handed over without complete training and weapon systems, and might not be fully operational until December 2035.
The audit found that trials and commissioning could not be completed on schedule, with five complementary contracts for weapons and support systems still incomplete.

The report said the most serious issue involved the ship’s surface-to-surface missiles, with deliveries delayed twice this year before supplies were halted following the suspension of the supplier’s export licence.
The audit also found that, as of June 25, the overall LCS project was 7.55% behind schedule across all five ships, with delays ranging from 30 to 108 days.
The LCS project, which had an original cost of RM9 billion, is said to be the largest defence procurement in Malaysia's history.
It came under intense scrutiny in 2022 after the Public Accounts Committee revealed that none of the six ships had been completed although Putrajaya had already paid out RM6.08 billion.
Due to delays and cost overruns, the project cost ballooned to RM11.22 billion while the number of vessels to be delivered was reduced from six to five.

According to the initial plan, the first ship was supposed to have been delivered in 2019. Under a revised plan, the vessels were scheduled to be delivered in August 2026, April and December 2027, August 2028, and April 2029.
79693112b9451e54: SHAH ALAM: The Road Transport Department (RTD) seized 14 vehicles during a two-hour enforcement operation in Jalan Teluk Menegun.
Selangor RTD director Datuk Ahmad Kamarunzaman Mehat said yesterday's operation involved 13 motorcycles and a three-wheeled motorcycle.
"The riders were Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Cambodian nationals who were found committing several road traffic offences.
"The offences detected included driving without a valid licence, expired motor vehicle licences and having no insurance coverage," he said when contacted today.
He said checks found that each rider had committed between four and five offences.
"The operation, dubbed Ops Pewa, was conducted from 11am to 1pm as part of a statewide crackdown on foreign nationals driving or riding vehicles in Selangor.
"Some of the riders attempted to delay enforcement action by giving various excuses.
"Some pretended that they needed to go to the toilet in an attempt to delay action being taken against them," he said.
He said some of the motorcycles belonged to the riders, while others were registered to different owners.
The vehicles were being used by the foreigners to travel to work and conduct business activities.
All 14 vehicles were seized and taken to the Selangor RTD enforcement office in Shah Alam for further action.
Ahmad Kamarunzaman said the department would continue monitoring complaints and carrying out enforcement to ensure vehicles and road users complied with traffic laws.
Members of the public can lodge complaints about traffic offences through the department's e-aduan platform or its traffic complaints email.

41ad1df057d5923c: PRAGUE, Oct 7 — Public broadcaster Czech TV said yesterday it would skip next year’s Eurovision Song Contest over spending cuts forced by a planned switch to financing from the state budget.

The nationalist government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis wants to switch from licence fees paid by viewers to direct government financing, to make Czech TV and public counterpart Czech Radio broadcaster save money.

Critics, including the Reporters Without Borders (RSF) press watchdog, say the move jeopardises the independence of public media, and Czech TV and Czech Radio staged a token strike over the plan in June.
“We won’t see the Czech flag on the stage next year,” Czech TV said on X, adding that it was hoping to return to the bling bonanza at some point.
“We know Eurovision means a lot for all of us. So we thank all Czech performers and above all you, fans, for each vote, each commentary, each cheer, and for being there,” it added.
The Czech decision is another financial blow to the European Broadcasting Union, which organises the world’s biggest live televised music event.

Ireland and Spain are expected to boycott Eurovision 2027 over the participation of Israel, with Irish broadcaster RTE citing “the appalling and ongoing loss of lives in Gaza and the humanitarian crisis there”.

Five European countries — the Netherlands, Iceland, Ireland, Slovenia and Spain — all snubbed this year’s showpiece, querying why Israel was allowed to participate despite its war on Palestinians in Gaza, while Russia had been suspended shortly after its invasion of Ukraine.
This year’s final on Czech TV attracted 287,000 viewers — a viewing share of 13.37 per cent.
No Czech performer has ever won Eurovision.
This year, Czech singer Daniel Zizka finished 16th with a song called Crossroads.
Babis’s critics have accused him of trying to curb the independence of public media, as did Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico and former Hungarian premier Viktor Orban.

The prime minister says the government coalition — comprising his catch-all ANO party, a far-right party and a right-wing one — is merely fulfilling its pledge to voters and trying to make Czech TV and Czech Radio cut costs.
Both outlets have already announced staff cuts and programme adjustments.
The Czech parliament, in which Babis’s coalition holds a majority, has yet to vote on the financing overhaul. — AFP
b6c690195b76f791: BENGALURU: HSBC is planning sweeping job cuts across its UK wealth management business as part of a push to expand its use of AI, the Financial Times reported yesterday.

The bank plans to cut about half of management and specialist roles, while reductions in financial adviser roles could reach around 70 per cent, the report said, citing people familiar with the plans.
HSBC does not disclose the number of employees in its UK wealth business, though the FT reported that it has hundreds of relationship managers across the country.
The bank did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.

"We're continuing to evolve to deliver more digitally enabled products and journeys to support our best-in-class wealth service and meet the changing needs of our customers," the bank said in a statement to the FT.
The bank is currently consulting employees on the proposed changes, the report said, adding that affected employees are expected to leave by the end of the month.
In May, chief executive Georges Elhedery said at an HSBC investor day event that staff needed to embrace AI-driven change rather than resist it and that "generative AI will destroy certain jobs".
Elhedery has made AI a central part of his strategy since taking over in 2024.
48fa83c7816096b7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Bursa Malaysia continued its downtrend at midday in line with regional markets amid persistent selling pressure and elevated oil prices.

Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) said Brent crude oil rose 0.5 per cent to about US$101 per barrel as Houthi missile and Iranian tanker attacks outweighed improving supply flows from Saudi Arabia and G7 reserves.
At the time of writing, Brent crude was up 1.02 per cent to US$101.60 a barrel.
“Focus this week shifts to third-quarter earnings, alongside Federal Open Market Committee minutes and preliminary October consumer sentiment,” HLIB said in a note today.

It said that ahead of Budget 2027 on October 9, United States-Iran tensions and a hawkish Federal Reserve narrative could keep the FBM KLCI in risk-off consolidation, amid elevated oil prices, surging bond yields and persistent foreign outflows.

Meanwhile, the Melaka polls could add to political uncertainty while offering clues on voter sentiment, coalition dynamics and seat negotiations, amid speculation of an early 16th general election, it said.

Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Public Bank decreased two sen each to RM9.89 and RM4.59, and CIMB fell 38 sen to RM7.32, while Tenaga Nasional added six sen to RM12.96 and IHH Healthcare was flat at RM7.91.

Nestle led the top decliners, falling RM1.56 to RM89.70, while Hong Leong Bank declined 62 sen to RM21.46, Fraser & Neave lost 58 sen to RM21.14, CIMB erased 38 sen to RM7.32, and Hong Leong Financial Group gave up 36 sen to RM17.98.

Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.19 of a point to 180.60, the Energy Index improved 3.50 points to 844.22, the Plantation Index shrank 57.92 points to 8,984.25, and the Financial Services Index retreated 477.86 points to 18,590.14. — Bernama
8988152538ccd163: MUMBAI: India's central bank hiked interest rates for the first time in more than three years on Wednesday as the Middle East conflict stokes inflation in Asia's third-largest economy and batters a weakened rupee.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said the benchmark repurchase rate, the level at which it lends to commercial banks, would be raised by 25 basis points to 5.50% after a unanimous vote by a six-member panel.
In doing so, the RBI shifted gears to join several central banks around the world who have raised rates to curb price rises or boost their currencies.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, the RBI has stood pat as it waited to assess the impact of volatile oil prices on the world's fastest-growing major economy.

But resilient GDP growth last quarter has allowed it to focus on higher costs in a country that imports most of its energy and has been hit by a weak monsoon that could result in a spike in food prices.

Retail inflation rose to 4.82% in August - the third straight month that headline inflation breached the RBI's medium term target of four percent - with data signalling that inflationary pressures had spread beyond food and transport.
Adding to the central bank's calculations is pressure on the Indian rupee, which has been at near record lows over the past week.
To stem the fall, the RBI has rolled out an array of moves to woo dollar inflows, including a deposit scheme for the Indian diaspora that raked in around US$127 billion.
While the steps helped stop the rupee's losses, the currency has faced fresh challenges as foreign investors continue to dump Indian equities and crude hovers around US$100 a barrel.
India, the world's third-largest buyer of oil, normally sources about half of its crude through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since the beginning of the Middle East war.
Analysts say this makes India among the most vulnerable economies to a global energy shock, as higher crude and fertiliser prices drive up the import bill.

"None of the suspects had previous criminal records," he said in a statement today.
Azry said police seized 14 mobile phones, seven computers, a laptop, two Wi-Fi routers and a vehicle during the series of raids yesterday.
The items were estimated to be worth about RM215,000.
"The syndicate was believed to be involved in an online investment scam targeting victims in China and Europe.

Drivers can shed up to three kilogrammes (more than six pounds) during the longest outing on the calendar, where completing the 62 steamy laps often lasts the maximum two hours race time allowed.
A floor upgrade coupled with Verstappen finally working out how to get the best from the new generation car led him to call the result at Sepang four days ago "amazing."
Runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second in the Mercedes and is likely to be challenging for the chequered flag again.

He was the beneficiary of yet more bad luck for his teammate and main title rival George Russell, who was "beyond disappointment" after an agonising power unit failure when running third with five laps to go in Malaysia.
"You've almost got to laugh... it's just so many times this season it's happened," said Russell, who has failed to finish three times in 16 grands prix so far in 2026.

Lewis Hamilton has won four times in Singapore in the past and was buoyed by a drive at Sepang where he cut through the field to recover to third after starting on unsuitable dry tyres and dropping to the back.
"To finish on the podium after the way the race began feels really satisfying," said Hamilton.
"It is a great reward for the hard work, determination and resilience everyone showed today."
Russell won the Singapore Grand Prix a year ago, edging Verstappen and the current world champion Lando Norris of McLaren. - AFP
3e53d250d68d35e2: PETALING JAYA: Wakil rakyat kerajaan dan pembangkang menggesa siasatan menyeluruh dilakukan berhubung kelewatan projek kapal tempur pesisir (LCS) Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia (TLDM), termasuk menerusi penubuhan Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI).

Ketika membahaskan Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (LKAN) 2026 di Dewan Rakyat, Ahmad Amzad Mohamed (PN-Kuala Terengganu) menyokong cadangan Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) supaya kerajaan menubuhkan RCI bagi menyiasat projek berkenaan.
Ahmad berkata sama ada melalui RCI atau mekanisme lain, siasatan mendalam perlu dilakukan memandangkan projek itu membabitkan dana awam dalam jumlah besar.
“Bertahun-tahun perkara ini dibangkitkan dan orang tertanya-tanya apa sebenarnya masalah.
“Saya setuju perlu ada siasatan mendalam. Kalau perlu RCI, buat RCI. Rakyat perlu penjelasan mengenai penggunaan dana awam ini,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, Hassan Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) berpandangan RCI tidak diperlukan kerana prosesnya mengambil masa dan lebih rumit.
Sebaliknya, beliau menggesa Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) dan polis segera menyiasat projek itu secara menyeluruh sejak 2013.
“Perlu tindakan segera. Siasat terus dari 2013 hingga 2026. Dalam tempoh 13 tahun ini, sudah lima kali kerajaan bertukar dan ada lima menteri pertahanan.

Isnin lalu, LKAN 2/2026 mendapati projek LCS lewat 7.55% daripada jadual setakat 25 Jun, sekali gus menimbulkan risiko terhadap penyerahan fizikal LCS 1.
Kelewatan itu antaranya berpunca daripada sistem pelancar Naval Strike Missile (NSM) yang masih belum tersedia selepas permit eksportnya dibatalkan secara kekal oleh kerajaan Norway.

Ketua Audit Negara Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi dilaporkan berkata kelewatan antara 30 hingga 108 hari itu boleh menjejaskan tarikh penyerahan yang dijadualkan pada 26 Ogos atau sasaran disemak pada 26 Disember.
Beliau berkata LCS 1 tidak akan mencapai keupayaan penuh sekiranya diserahkan sebelum latihan dan sistem persenjataannya diselesaikan.
Kelewatan kapal pertama itu juga dijangka memberi kesan kepada jadual penyerahan LCS 2 hingga LCS 5.
Sementara itu, Ikmal Hisham Abdul Aziz (PN-Tanah Merah) berkata kelewatan pembinaan LCS tidak lagi mengejutkan kerana isu itu sudah berulang kali dibangkitkan di Dewan Rakyat.
Katanya, LKAN 2026 menunjukkan penyerahan fizikal LCS pertama sekali lagi berdepan kelewatan, daripada Disember 2026 kepada April 2027.
“Dari satu tarikh ke satu tarikh baharu. Laporan audit sekali lagi mengesahkan berlaku peralihan ‘tiang gol’ bagi penyerahan fizikal kapal LCS pertama.
“Kementerian Pertahanan perlu beri penjelasan, bukan hanya mahu menjaga hati kontraktor,” katanya.
b41f7cecadb9ea54: STOCKHOLM, Oct 7 — Molecules that regulate sleep and appetite or methods for editing genes are some of the research fields commentators say could be contenders for the Nobel Prize in Chemistry announced today.
The winner or winners of the award are scheduled to be named by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm at 11.45am (0945 GMT/5.45pm Malaysian time).
Last year, the jury honoured Japan’s Susumu Kitagawa, UK-born Richard Robson and American-Jordanian Omar Yaghi for developing a method of designing molecular structures.

This year, data analytics firm Clarivate predicted that research into the hunger-regulating hormone glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) was a contender for the Nobel Prize in Medicine on Monday — but that award went to neuroscientists.
However GLP-1, which is used in weight-loss drugs such as Wegovy and Mounjaro, “could receive a chemistry prize”, said David Pendlebury, who heads research analysis at Clarivate.

While many scientists have made significant contributions in the field, three regularly mentioned for the Nobel are Canadian endocrinologist Daniel Drucker, Danish physician Jens Juul Holst and Yugoslav-born American chemist Svetlana Mojsov.

For chemistry, Clarivate this year also spotlighted the development of “self-assembled monolayers (SAMs)” — molecular-scale coatings that allow scientists and engineers to tailor a surface’s properties.
US chemists David Allara and Ralph Nuzzo along with Israel’s Jacob Sagiv would then be favourites. — AFP
7b2b67d9cab9edb3: COVENTRY: Jaguar presented the first model of its new fully electric lineup, a £130,000 (US$172,000) grand tourer aimed at breathing new life into the storied British brand.

Orders for the Type 01 will open in early 2027, more than two years after Jaguar stopped selling new cars in the UK as part of a decision to overhaul the marque with new branding and limit it to luxury EVs.
It will target younger customers — a change for a nameplate known for being popular with middle-aged men and the go-to car for British prime ministers.
The new model, the first in eight years, arrives at a key moment for Jaguar after a radical rebranding in 2024 was met with criticism.
A video released at the time to build anticipation prompted mixed reviews when it was devoid of vehicles and featured expressionless fashion models.
First—look footage of the Type 01 published on YouTube has also triggered a range of responses, including “boring” and “looks like a generic modern Chinese EV,” as well as “beautiful” and “fabulous”.
The official unveiling on Tuesday evening in New York follows similarly mixed receptions for other luxury EVs.

Ferrari NV’s first electric model, the Luce, was widely panned, while Volkswagen AG’s Bentley brand sought to steer clear of design controversy by sticking with a traditional look for its first fully battery-powered car.

Unlike Ferrari, Jaguar was in need of a drastic reboot. Its parent, Jaguar Land Rover Automotive Plc (JLR), owned by India’s Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd, had for years focused on its more profitable Land Rover and Range Rover sport utility vehicles with growing sales in the US.
By contrast, the Jaguar brand was fading, with annual sales of 66,900 in its final full year before it went into hibernation.
That was barely a third of what it produced after it launched the I-Pace, its most recent new model, in 2018.
Still, halting production completely is an unusual move from a carmaker, even when it’s overhauling the brand.
Jaguar ended production of all its models in 2024, apart from F-Pace SUVs, which it continued to make in the UK for export.

Jaguar, which traces its roots to 1922 and is known for classic cars like the iconic E-Type, “is a vital part of JLR’s growth story,” CEO PB Balaji said in a statement. The company initially announced its EV-only direction in early 2021.
It picked a venue in New York for the unveiling as it sees the US as a key market for the Type 01.
That’s as EV skepticism among US buyers remains entrenched, including at the luxury end of the market.

Even in Europe, where EVs are more prevalent, there’s still some nervousness about going fully electric, though sales have risen this year due to higher fuel prices and thanks to the return of incentives in key countries like Germany.
Some European brands, such as VW and Mercedes-Benz Group AG, have dialed back early pronouncements about making exclusively EVs after demand waned, only to find it recovering again.
The Jaguar Type 01 will be made at its Solihull plant, with electric drive units and battery packs produced in nearby Wolverhampton.
The EV will travel as far as 400 miles (644km) on a single charge, with 200 miles of range added in 13 minutes with rapid charging. The Type 01 can reach 62 miles per hour in 3.2 seconds.
The new Jaguar is “another big vote of confidence in our world-class automotive industry,” UK business secretary Jonathan Reynolds said in a statement.
It follows recent investment pledges by McLaren Automotive Ltd and Nissan Motor Co.

At the same time, JLR is cutting around 4,000 jobs as Britain’s largest carmaker grapples with challenges including US tariffs, the fallout from a cyberattack that crippled production, and intense competition, including from Chinese manufacturers. It also just unveiled its first electric Range Rover.
The new Jaguar brand is only expected to produce in small volumes, rather than return to historic levels.
adaf6c815a9b7360: SINGAPORE: Singapore has proposed two initiatives to strengthen Asean's response to online scams as it assumes Asean's chairmanship next year, Singapore's senior minister K. Shanmugam said on Tuesday, reported Xinhua.

As the Asean Voluntary Lead Shepherd for cybercrime and online scams, Singapore proposed an Asean code of practice to combat scams on online platforms, which would establish voluntary baseline safeguards that member states can adapt and apply to online platforms to detect, prevent and disrupt scams, he said in a written reply to a parliamentary question.
The proposed safeguards include timely escalation of detected scam activity to relevant authorities and reasonable verification measures to prevent inauthentic accounts from being used for scams.
Singapore also proposed an Asean Best Practices Guide covering scam investigations, legislation and public education, Shanmugam said.

The initiatives complement multilateral efforts such as "FRONTIER+," which was mooted by the Singapore Police Force and supports intelligence sharing, joint enforcement and cross-border fund tracing and asset freezing.
Six Asean members currently participate in FRONTIER+, Shanmugam added.
f47458564a229033: KUALA LUMPUR: The two Special Branch policemen allegedly assaulted by Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Suhaily Mohd Zain at KLIA have denied claims that they were acting as touts or involved in 'counter setting'.

Their lawyers, Kamal Hisham & Associates, said any such allegation must be supported by evidence and should not be used to divert attention from the alleged assault involving lance corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman and Mohammad Faiz Muhamad.
The firm said the two policemen were carrying out official duties at KLIA1 when the alleged incident took place on Sept 28.
It claimed that both men were physically assaulted by Suhaily in a public area, causing them injuries and affecting their dignity as civil servants carrying out their duties.
The firm said that MCBA was not part of the police force and that the two agencies had different functions and jurisdictions.
It said statements had since emerged on social media and through official channels which, according to its clients, portrayed a different version of what had happened.
The firm said any public statement concerning a matter still under investigation should be made responsibly and should not prejudice the ongoing probe.
"We deny any portrayal that our clients acted as touts or were involved in any counter-setting.

"Any such allegation must be supported by evidence and should not be used to divert attention from the main issue, namely the allegation that Suhaily had physically assaulted Ekmal and Faiz," it said.
The firm said based on the facts and evidence being presented to the authorities, the alleged incident could potentially involve Sections 186 and 323 of the Penal Code.
Section 186 deals with obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties, while Section 323 concerns voluntarily causing hurt.

However, the firm said it would leave it to the authorities to conduct an independent, transparent and comprehensive investigation and determine whether any offence had been committed based on the evidence gathered.
It called for the investigation to be carried out transparently, independently and promptly, and for appropriate legal action to be taken based on the findings and evidence.
The lawyers also advised the public not to draw conclusions based on unverified narratives and to allow the authorities to complete their investigation.
The two policemen maintained that they were carrying out official duties at the time of the incident and were entitled to protection and justice under the law.
Yesterday, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said he had received the investigation papers from the police, who recorded statements from 25 witnesses to assist in the probe.
He said the Attorney-General's Chambers would examine witness statements, closed-circuit television footage and other evidence before deciding on further action over the incident.
845723d40f6d3754: MELAKA: Following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly, the state administration enters a transition phase governed by constitutional protocols and election regulations.
The following is a step-by-step breakdown of what happens next and how the caretaker government operates:
1. The 60-day constitutional window
Under the Melaka State Constitution, a state election must be conducted within 60 days from the date of the assembly's dissolution.
Notification: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly will formally notify the Election Commission (EC) of the dissolution.
Election Commission (EC) special meeting: The EC will convene a special meeting to fix key dates:
Writ of election: Official notice announcing the poll.
Nomination day: Candidate registration (typically 10 to 14 days after the meeting).
Campaign period: Must run for a minimum of 11 days.
Early voting and polling day: Date set for regular and early voters.
2. Caretaker government rules
From the moment of dissolution until a new chief minister is sworn in, the existing state executive council (exco) functions strictly as a caretaker government.
What a caretaker government can do:
- Carry out routine administrative duties to ensure government services run uninterrupted.
- Respond to emergencies, natural disasters, or public health crises.
- Implement previously approved policies and budget allocations already passed in the State assembly.
What a caretaker government cannot do:
- Make major policy decisions or sign binding long-term state contracts.
- Announce major financial allocations or new development projects aimed at influencing voters.
- Utilise state assets, official vehicles, or government machinery for political campaigning.
3. What happens on polling day?

Once voting concludes, results are tallied across the 28 state seats. The party or coalition that secures at least 15 seats will be invited by the Yang di-Pertua Negeri to form the government and present their chief minister candidate.

c81c188b183250cf: MUMBAI, Oct 7 — India’s central bank hiked interest rates for the first time in more than three years today as the Middle East conflict stokes inflation in Asia’s third-largest economy and batters a weakened rupee.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said the benchmark repurchase rate, the level at which it lends to commercial banks, would be raised by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent after a unanimous vote by a six-member panel.
In doing so, the RBI shifted gears to join several central banks around the world who have raised rates to curb price rises or boost their currencies.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, the RBI has stood pat as it waited to assess the impact of volatile oil prices on the world’s fastest-growing major economy.

But resilient GDP growth last quarter has allowed it to focus on higher costs in a country that imports most of its energy and has been hit by a weak monsoon that could result in a spike in food prices.

Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August — the third straight month that headline inflation breached the RBI’s medium-term target of four per cent — with data signalling that inflationary pressures had spread beyond food and transport.
Adding to the central bank’s calculations is pressure on the Indian rupee, which has been at near record lows over the past week.
To stem the fall, the RBI has rolled out an array of moves to woo dollar inflows, including a deposit scheme for the Indian diaspora that raked in around US$127 billion (RM520 billion).
While the steps helped stop the rupee’s losses, the currency has faced fresh challenges as foreign investors continue to dump Indian equities and crude hovers around US$100 a barrel.
India, the world’s third-largest buyer of oil, normally sources about half of its crude through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since the beginning of the Middle East war.
Analysts say this makes India among the most vulnerable economies to a global energy shock, as higher crude and fertiliser prices drive up the import bill. — AFP
a11dd7567516fdd0: KUALA LUMPUR: Contractor management weaknesses were behind 77 per cent of 33 "sick projects" under the Public Works Department (JKR) as of Sept 30.

92af452d02228b53: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The park is just across Sungai Bonus, but for children at the Wangsa Sari People's Housing Programme here, getting there has meant balancing along water pipes.
By the end of this year, they should be able to simply walk across, with an 18-metre-long, two-metre-wide pedestrian bridge expected to be completed behind the 21-storey block.
It will lead to Padang Wangsa Sari and reduce the need for residents to use the narrower Jalan 2/27A.
Resident Mohd Fazil Md Noor, 56, said it would also give children a safer and easier way to get to SK Wangsa Maju Section 1, where some currently walk or cycle.
“We really need the bridge that is going to be built because once it is completed, it will become the main route for our children to get to and from school.

“The school is less than 5km from this PPR. If they cross the bridge, it will be much closer, perhaps cutting about 1km off the journey. Some of our children walk or cycle to school, so building this bridge is really ideal. This is something we have been hoping for,” he told Malay Mail when met today.
The idea began when Wangsa Maju MP Zahir Hassan visited the area in 2023 and found that residents of the flats had limited access to recreational facilities despite a park being across the river.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Wangsa Sari PPR resident Jasbee Kaur, 67, speaks to Malay Mail about the planned pedestrian bridge and the facelift. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
“After winning the 2022 general election, when I came here in 2023, we walked around the area and found that there were not enough facilities.
“We saw that there was a park across the river and asked how we could make maximum use of the park,” he told Malay Mail during a visit today.
Zahir said he later raised the matter with Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud, after learning that children had fallen into the river while attempting to cross using the water pipes.

“When the children had fallen, they did not think of it as a tragedy because they fell into the water, but it was dangerous. We were worried about what would happen if the water level was high,” he said.
Fadlun said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) had allocated an additional RM200,000 for the bridge and would try to expedite its construction for completion before the end of the year.
Once complete, the bridge is expected to serve all 1,061 residents and encourage greater use of the park for exercise and community activities.

Another resident, Jasbee Kaur, 67, who has lived at the Wangsa Sari flats – commonly known by the abbreviation PPR for Projek Perumahan Rakyat – for 19 years, said residents had welcomed the bridge, which she believed would make it easier for children to return home from the park.
“The bridge is needed. When the children are tired, they will have a shortcut to come home and it will be easier for them to enter the taman next door,” she said.
However, 53-year-old resident Nurazlina Abd Aziz said safety concerns would remain once the bridge is completed, particularly with motorcycles parked behind the block.
“Many motorcycles are parked at the back, so there may be an increase in theft. If the children want to go to school, yes, but we also have to think about their safety,” she said.
The bridge is part of a wider facelift for Wangsa Sari PPR, which was built in 2008 and has 272 residential units housing about 1,061 residents.
The block, previously painted entirely white, now has a two-tone beige and white colour scheme under a RM2.24 million upgrading project covering the building and its basic infrastructure.

Of the allocation, RM1.1 million was spent on repainting the building, RM904,000 on replacing the sub-main cable and main switchboard, RM136,000 on road resurfacing and RM101,000 on upgrading the fire safety system.

Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said one of the reforms introduced was allowing MPs, through a committee set up to monitor DBKL spending, to provide feedback on how the city hall allocates funds.

“With feedback from all these MPs, our spending is more transparent and also meets the needs of residents. So, we do not have wasteful expenditure because all of this involves basic infrastructure needed by residents,” she said.
She said the repainting was also intended to improve the dignity of PPR residents, with the new neutral colour scheme selected by Fadlun.
“I agree that PPR buildings are usually painted in too many colours, to the point that they look like kindergartens. But now, all the colours are neutral and look nice,” she said.
Fadlun said DBKL had completed almost 70 per cent of upgrading projects involving the city’s 64 PPR and public housing schemes under the RM300 million allocation this year.
He said expenditure was expected to reach 90 per cent of the allocation by year-end, with about RM23 million to be carried forward to complete the remaining projects.
Fazil, who has lived at the PPR for about 15 years, said the makeover felt like a festive occasion.
“Our buildings have also been repainted. It feels like Hari Raya, everything looks new, Alhamdulillah. The wiring and lights have also been replaced, and we have seen the improvements,” he said.
Jasbee, asked about Fazil’s Hari Raya description, laughed and gave the makeover her own festive comparison.
“For me, it’s like Deepavali!” she said.
She said the improvements had also brought a renewed sense of community among residents, whom she described as cooperative and supportive of one another.
“Our residents are very cooperative. We stick with each other,” she said.
Still, she has one request for the government.
“We want the government to open up the opportunity for us to buy these homes. We are still renting them. We need to be able to buy them,” she said.
e2863319ac5dc5df: JEDDAH: Early strikes secured hosts Saudi Arabia the 27th Gulf Cup with a 2-0 win over the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday, ending a 22-year wait to lift the trophy again.
Winger Hammam Al Hammami opened the scoring in the 11th minute with a deflected shot from the edge of the box, sparking celebrations at King Abdullah Sports City in Jeddah.

Just two minutes later, Georgios Donis' side took a 2-0 lead when Feras Al Brikan struck from close range. They almost scored again when Saleh Abu Alshamat, who started alongside his brother Mohammed, hit the bar.
"We are very happy... there were many difficulties, but the players showed concentration and discipline and gave their maximum on the pitch," Donis told a press conference.

"I think we turned those difficulties into a title, and that is important. We were the best team in this competition. This title gives us confidence for the future, and we have to keep showing the same qualities" he added.
The UAE pressed to try to close the deficit. They were awarded a penalty in the 38th minute only to see the VAR overturn the decision.

After the interval, Saudi goalkeeper Mohamed Al Owais denied Sultan Adil from close range and Fabio Lima struck the bar in the 88th minute, leaving Saudi Arabia with a clean sheet throughout the tournament.
The triumph followed an early and disappointing exit from this year's World Cup and gave the Saudis a fourth Gulf Cup title, their first since 2004.

"After the World Cup, we knew that we had made mistakes and had some bad moments, but we learned from this experience... we improved and developed our football. And I think they deserve this result. Now, the result reflects the work" said Donis.
Saudi Arabia will take on Kuwait, Oman and Palestine at the 2027 Asian Cup on home soil, with the tournament scheduled for January 7-February 5.

"We have an even bigger challenge ahead, which is the Asian Cup. God willing, this (title) will give us even greater motivation to do what satisfies the national team and Saudi as a whole," Player of the Tournament Al Hammami told Alkass Sports TV.-Reuters
